audit.whatIsWrong: early says "if you force him to spend Fury on the gap-close rather than the W-heal"; whys[1] says he has no heal "without spending Fury on W"; wants.foe[0] describes "a full-Fury Spinning Slash".
audit.why: Two errors compounded. His heal is Bloodlust, which is Q, not W — W is Mocking Shout. And Fury is consumed only by Bloodlust: Spinning Slash costs nothing and consumes no Fury, so there is no Fury tug-of-war between gap-close and heal to force. Full Fury does not empower Spinning Slash either; it is crit chance, which powers his basic attacks.
audit.corrected: Bloodlust (Q) is the heal and the only Fury consumer, 12s. Spinning Slash (E) is free. Full Fury = crit chance on autos.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tryndamere.json (P Battle Fury, Q Bloodlust, W Mocking Shout, E Spinning Slash cost 0)

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry treats the blind purely as damage negation and never connects it to his resource.
audit.why: Battle Fury is generated by attacks, crits and killing blows, and Bloodlust is the only thing that spends Fury — on healing. So a blind does not just delete a damage window, it starves the Fury that would have paid for the heal afterwards. That double effect is the reason repeated blind-trades compound against Tryndamere instead of merely trading evenly, and no field in the entry says it.
audit.corrected: Blind starves him twice — no autos means no damage and no Fury, so Bloodlust has nothing to convert.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid says "Q is max-ranked (shortest cooldown)"; whys[3] "Max-rank Q cooldown lets you blind nearly every spin cycle"; spikes[1].text "Q is max-ranked".
audit.why: Blinding Dart is a flat 7s at every rank — ranking it up buys blind duration, never a shorter cooldown. The conclusion these fields reach is right but the reason is wrong: you answer nearly every spin because Spinning Slash is 12/11/10/9/8s and your 7s blind simply undercuts it. Stating the real pair of numbers is what makes the advice checkable in game.
audit.corrected: Blinding Dart 7s flat vs Spinning Slash 12s at rank 1 — the blind undercuts the gap-close, at every rank.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3].text and the full layer both treat Undying Rage as a constant threat without a timer.
audit.why: Undying Rage is 120/100/80s. At rank 1 that is a two-minute window between comeback tools, which is the difference between "never chase" and "chase freely for the next ninety seconds" — the single most actionable number in the matchup after the blind.

mid already has the Mocking Shout directional tech right — the move-speed slow only applies to enemies with their backs turned, so briefly turning into him breaks it. That matches Riot's text exactly and is genuinely good detail; I left it and only tightened the wording.

edits.before: At level 1 Tryndamere has exactly one plan: build Fury on minions, then Spinning Slash onto you and auto. Fire Blinding Shot the instant he lands — his spin puts him in melee range and his entire DPS window is basic attacks, so the blind erases it completely. He cannot meaningfully retaliate. Hit him once with a poisoned auto, walk back, and do it again before his Fury regenerates. He has no level 1 heal yet if you force him to spend Fury on the gap-close rather than the W-heal, so each blind-trade chips him without return damage.
edits.after: At level 1 Tryndamere has exactly one plan: build Fury on minions, then Spinning Slash onto you and auto. Fire Blinding Dart the instant he lands — his spin puts him in melee range and his entire DPS window is basic attacks, so the blind erases it completely. He cannot meaningfully retaliate. Hit him once with a poisoned auto, walk back, and do it again. The blind starves him twice over: Fury is built by attacking, and Bloodlust is the only thing that spends it, so a blanked trade costs him the damage and the heal that would have paid for it.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your cleanest control window: Q is max-ranked (shortest cooldown), your poison is ticking on him almost continuously, and shrooms in the tribush and river entrance mean he cannot flank to bait the blind before spinning. When he uses Mocking Shout to slow you after a trade, move toward him briefly — the slow drops off enemies that face him, not away — to break the slow and maintain your spacing. Track his Fury bar; if he gets to 100 and his E is up, respect the all-in threat and pre-place a shroom where he would land to slow his follow-through. His R is not a kill yet at this stage but do not chase a low-HP Tryndamere into a bush — shroom it first, then push him into it.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your cleanest control window: your blind is a flat 7s against Spinning Slash's 12s at rank 1, your poison is ticking on him almost continuously, and shrooms in the tribush and river entrance mean he cannot flank to bait the blind before spinning.
